summary: Iteration 26 — Transactional email system on top of Resend. Backend: 25/25 tests passed (1 skipped — report_received test could not find a target user via /demo-accounts endpoint). Frontend: Email Preferences screen (6 toggles) works and persists after reload; Control Centre → Emails page shows Templates (56 rows, 33 mandatory, mandatory switches disabled), Events (search + status chips + rows), Failures & Bounces (KPIs 0 Sent / 29 Failed / 6 Suppressed / 6 Bounced + scheduler last-run timestamp + Retry table + Suppressions table), Preview modal renders full branded HTML in iframe + Send test input. All Resend deliveries return HTTP 403 'orrbbit.com domain is not verified' — expected. Password-reset regression preserved (event logged, wrong code → 400). Bounce webhook x2 correctly suppresses; complained suppresses immediately; DELETE suppression works. Mandatory templates cannot be disabled (400). Security emails (password_reset/verify_email) cannot be retried (400). Demo login + real login regression OK; professional endpoints alive.

minor.issue: Cooldown check only inspects status='sent' events. Because Resend returns 403 on this env, first send is 'failed' -> 60-min cooldown never engages, so identical feedbacks logged again as new events. This is by-design (failed sends don't block retries per agent note), but once the domain is verified real users could still trigger duplicate feedback emails until the first one succeeds. Consider counting 'failed' toward cooldown or gating on 'sent OR failed' for cooldown-only checks.

issues: Layout clean and mobile-friendly (icons + labels + descriptions + switches, minHeight 64px, ~44px touch targets).

action_items: Optional: adjust cooldown check in email_service.py to also consider 'failed' rows (or gate on 'sent OR failed' for cooldown_min>0 templates) so once Resend is unblocked the intended 60-min cooldown on feedback_received still holds even if a prior send hit a transient failure.
Cleanup: several TEST_emailtest_*@gmail.com users and TEST_ feedback rows were created during testing. If desired, main agent can delete them or add a teardown fixture.

Security review: POST /api/webhooks/resend is unauthenticated. Recommend Resend signing-secret verification before enabling in production (currently any client can mutate suppressions via crafted payloads).
critical_code_review_comments: email_service.py cleanly separates preferences / cooldown / idempotency / rate-limit / suppression checks and never logs codes/tokens (CTX_SAFE_KEYS whitelist is good).
control_email.py correctly guards mandatory-toggle (400) and security-retry (400). NO_RETRY = {password_reset, verify_email} — good.
Resend webhook is unauthenticated (POST /api/webhooks/resend). Consider adding a Resend signing-secret verification header before production.
PUT /users/me/email-preferences accepts partial updates via Optional bool fields — good, matches PATCH semantics.
email-preferences.tsx has optimistic UI (rollback on error) and clean testIDs (email-pref-<key>, email-pref-switch-<key>).
control/emails.tsx: iframe uses srcDoc (web-only) — mobile falls back to plain text preview, acceptable for admin.
email_scheduler.py runs every 300s and stores last_run in db.config — visible in Failures & Bounces tab (verified: 2026-07-29 04:17:39).

success_rate.backend: 100% (25/25 executed passed, 1 skipped due to missing target user id)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (email-preferences + control emails all 3 tabs + preview modal verified)
